walkthroughs.body_html:
Humans have 46 chromosomes — 23 pairs (22 autosomes + XX/XY).

Each chromosome is a single DNA molecule wrapped around histones into nucleosomes.

A karyotype displays them by size; trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) is detected this way.

Meiosis I separates homologous pairs:
- Prophase I — synapsis + crossing over at chiasmata.
- Metaphase I — bivalents align (independent assortment).
- Anaphase I — homologues separate.

Meiosis II separates sister chromatids (like mitosis). Result: 4 haploid cells.

Three mechanisms shuffle alleles in sexual reproduction:

1. Crossing over — new allele combinations on a chromosome.
2. Independent assortment — 2²³ possible gametes in humans (≈8.4 million).
3. Random fertilisation — any sperm meets any egg.
